subject: Re: Novaretail performance SLOs post-call recap & cost/perf levers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Novaretail performance SLOs - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Emma - great to chat this morning. Thanks for walking through Novaretail's real-time product search use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a config that hits your latency SLO while keeping unit cost reasonable.

Recap of requirements you confirmed on the call:
- Target user-facing latency: P95 <= 350ms for 1-3 streaming chunks on typical queries (avg response ~120 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~150-250 requests/sec during peak campaigns (90th percentile load)
- Expected concurrency: 40-60 simultaneous open connections per region
- Streaming: chunked responses required (partial results asap - first-byte latency matters)
- Quality: generation quality should match current GPT-3.5-like baseline for ranking + assistant responses

Immediate risks / unknowns we flagged:
- Query length distribution: need sample histograms for prompt sizes (especially long product descriptions)
- Tokenization & max output: clarify typical max generation length per request
- Cold-start tolerance: do you have strict cold-start SLOs for new model instances?

Cost / performance levers we'll explore (high level):
1) Continuous batching: reduces per-token compute by aggregating in-flight requests; we can tune batching window to balance latency vs throughput.
2) Prefix / KV caching: if many queries reuse the same prompt prefix (catalog context), we can cache KV states to avoid recomputing.
3) Quantization profiles: recommend testing 8-bit (int8) and 4-bit (q4) profiles on your representative prompts to measure quality delta vs throughput gain.
4) Model variants: provide a 13B quantized variant for production and a 7B variant for burst/preview traffic where slightly lower quality is acceptable.
5) Smart routing & fallback: route non-critical traffic to cheaper capacity or regionally distribute to keep user-facing latency consistent.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll run an initial capacity/config recommendation (expected throughput and 95th latency estimates) and share a one-page config that maps SLO -> recommended model/quantization/batch settings. (Deliverable: Redwood config PDF)
- You to share a small sample of real requests (anonymized) + token length distribution by EOD Friday so we can run representative perf tests.
- Follow-up call: 30 minutes next week to review the config and perf estimates.

I've attached a short template for the SLO/traffic sample (novaretail_slo_requirements.pdf). I'll follow up with a recommended config and expected cost delta by noon PT tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- The 350ms P95 target is end-to-end (client visible), including small network variance - is that realistic with streaming enabled for ~120-token responses?
- For concurrency: our current peak is 55 open sockets per region; planning for 60 to be safe.

Subject: Re: Novaretail performance SLOs - config recs & cost levers (details)

Hi Emma - thanks, got the sample set. Below are our recommended levers with expected trade-offs and a preliminary ROI view. I ran quick internal sims against the sample (representative prompts). Detailed perf runs will follow once we run on dedicated test infra.

1) Continuous batching
- Recommendation: enable continuous batching with a max micro-batch latency of 25ms and a max batch size of 64 tokens-equivalent.
- Expected effect: 20-40% reduction in effective GPU compute per token for steady-state workloads; adds <25ms median added queuing latency when under 60 concurrent connections.
- Risk: for sparse low-concurrency windows you get less benefit; use dynamic policy (drop to single-request exec below 8 concurrent).

2) Prefix / KV caching
- Recommendation: cache KV states for the common product-context prefix (TTL 10 minutes).
- Expected effect: for queries reusing catalog prefixes we see up to 60% CPU/GPU savings on prefix recompute and 50-70ms faster first-chunk times.
- Data needed: list of top 50 prefixes and their reuse frequency.

3) Quantization profiles
- Recommendation: test q8_0 (int8) and q4_0 (4-bit) profiles; deploy q8_0 for ranking models and q4_0 for non-critical preview flows during off-peak.
- Expected effect: q8_0 gives ~1.8x throughput increase; q4_0 can give 2.8-3.2x but with higher risk of subtle quality differences.
- Plan: run A/B on 5% traffic to validate no measurable drop in ranking metrics.

4) Model variants and routing
- Recommendation: primary: Redwood-13B-q8 (production ranker), secondary/burst: Redwood-7B-q4 for preview/batch tasks.
- Expected effect: ~35-50% cost savings on preview traffic when routing to the 7B variant; keeps primary quality intact.

5) Smart routing & regional capacity
- Recommendation: reserve baseline capacity to meet cold-start constraints (we can reserve a small pool of warm model instances) and use burst pools for transient spikes. Route by latency SLO: sensitive traffic to warm pool, best-effort to burst.

Preliminary numbers (very rough) vs unquantized single-model baseline:
- Expected cost delta (monthly) for target peak: ~0.6-0.8x (i.e., 20-40% savings) if we combine batching + q8 + caching + routing.
- Expected P95 latency: with recommended config we estimate end-to-end P95 ~260-330ms based on your sample distribution (streaming enabled).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Draft config PDF with recommended instance counts, batch params, and estimated TPS/latency by 12:00 PT tomorrow (attached: redwood-config-recommendation.pdf).
- Perf run on dedicated infra using your sample set once you confirm anonymized data - takes ~48 hours.
- Follow-up 30-min review next Wed (I'll share a calendar invite).

If this looks good I'll include explicit A/B experiment steps and a fallback policy (auto-failover to unquantized model if quality regression > threshold).

Best,
Marissa
